Donald Trump Accused of Bribing Voters With $5K Payout
Donald Trump Promises $5K To American Adults Who Vote For GOP In Midterms, Critics Slam It As An Obvious “Bribe”
Donald Trump and the rest of the MAGA Republicans know they are in trouble in the upcoming midterm elections, so desperate times call for desperate measures.

Donald Trump and the rest of the MAGA Republicans know they are in trouble in the upcoming midterm elections, so desperate times call for desperate measures.
During his almost 2-hour meandering speech at Trumpalooza, aka the GOP midterm convention in Texas, the orange menace promised that his administration would pay a $5,000 “Trump Dividend” to every American adult if voters stupidly deliver a Republican victory in the midterm elections.
“If the Republicans win, you win with us, and you get $5,000,” Trump told his gullible supporters at the convention, which many political experts are calling a clear sign Republicans are in trouble. “We’ll call it the Trump Dividend. Congratulations.”
If that sounds like a bribe, well, that’s because it is, and many people are describing it as such.
Sam Stein, managing editor at The Bulwark, also called Trump’s latest promise a flat-out “bribe.”
“Trump openly bribing people to vote for Republicans. $5k per person if republicans hold the House and the Senate?” Stein said in his post on X (formerly Twitter).
They are using the moment to remind us of his other financial promise that never came to fruition: the $2,000 tariff dividend check we are still waiting for.
Trump defended his bribery plan in an interview with Fox News’ Laura Ingraham, claiming the payments would be possible because of his stupid tariffs.
“We’re taking in 21 trillion dollars. No country has ever taken in anywhere near that,” Trump told Ingraham. “That’s four-five times more than the next. That’s all because of that beautiful word you and I love more tha most others- tariffs.”
We are truly living in some stupid times.
You can see more reactions to Trump bribing Americans in hopes of staying in power below.

Trump plan to send $5K to every adult projected to cost $1.2T and ‘explode’ the deficit
President Donald Trump speaks during an event at the White House on Aug. 6, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images)
WASHINGTON — A proposal by President Donald Trump to give $5,000 to each American adult if Republicans retain control of the U.S. House and Senate in November would “explode” the national deficit and worsen inflation, according to an analysis issued Thursday by the nonpartisan Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget.
The committee, whose board includes economists, bankers and former elected and administration officials from both political parties, estimates Trump’s plan would cost roughly $1.2 trillion.
“This proposal is fiscally dangerous, economically backwards, and fundamentally unserious,” Maya MacGuineas, the committee’s president, said in a statement. “It’s hard to understand how anyone could look at our current fiscal and economic situation and think we need to borrow another $1.2 trillion to send everyone cash.”
Trump announced the “Trump dividend” Wednesday night during the latter half of a nearly two-hour keynote speech at the Republican National Committee’s first midterm convention.
Trump told attendees at the political gathering in Dallas, Texas, that his “only caveat” is that Americans spend the money in the United States.
“We don’t want you going to Canada to spend the money,” he said during the livestreamed speech.
Ultimately, Congress would need to appropriate the funds.
Debt, deficits, inflation
MacGuineas pointed out in her statement that the nation’s debt “is now as large as our entire economy, deficits are running $2 trillion per year, inflation is about 3.5%, and the 10-year Treasury yield is approaching 5%.”
“This half-baked political scheme would make this all worse – exploding the deficit, ginning up inflation, and further driving up the cost of borrowing throughout the economy.”
The national debt sits at $40 trillion to date, which breaks down to $117,446 per taxpayer, according to a tracker by the Peter G. Peterson Foundation.
Vice President JD Vance said on Fox News following Trump’s speech that the dividend would be funded by tariff revenue.
“What the president’s just saying is … if you keep us in power and allow us to continue to do these things, then you’re going to share in some of the benefit of this incredible wealth that we’re creating in the United States of America,” he said to Fox News host Bret Baier.
But the expected revenue generated by Trump’s executive tariffs would only cover one-tenth of the cost of sending $5,000 to each American adult, according to an analysis Thursday from the Tax Foundation.
The organization that identifies itself as pro-economic growth, and generally opposes tax increases, estimates Trump’s new tariffs will bring in roughly $124.9 billion in 2027.
“A deficit-financed dividend payment of this scale would signal to markets that the US is not serious about getting its fiscal house in order. It would risk further rises in interest rates, add to inflationary pressures, and worsen the very problems that are trying to be ‘solved’ by the proposal,” said Erica York, a senior economist with the Tax Foundation, in a written statement. The organization opposes Trump’s tariff policies.
Tariff promises
This is not Trump’s first time promising to send what he describes as dividends to Americans — though none of the payments materialized.
The president said in November 2025 he would send $2,000 to Americans from tariff revenue that he falsely said would reach “trillions” of dollars.
Trump’s emergency tariffs were struck down by the Supreme Court in February, and the government is in the process of refunding nearly $170 billion in illegal import taxes.
Trump and then-special government employee and billionaire Elon Musk said in March 2025 they would send $5,000 refund checks to Americans as a result of savings created by the project titled the Department of Government Oversight. The ultrawealthy tech mogul went public with his plan without consultation from Congress, which controls the nation’s proverbial purse strings.
In spring of 2020, Trump’s name appeared on $1,200 stimulus checks for individuals, $2,400 for married couples, sent out as part of a $2.2 trillion initial COVID-19 relief package approved by Congress.

Trump and Vance's Plan To Bribe Voters With $5,000 Checks Shows MAGA Is Out of Ideas
By quickly endorsing Trump's ridiculous plan to bribe voters in the midterms, J.D. Vance reveals something about the future of Trumpism. There isn't one.
Not long after President Donald Trump offered to bribe voters to back Republicans in this year's midterm elections, Vice President J.D. Vance was asked about the idea by Fox News' Bret Baier.
Vance's response is, in many ways, more important than Trump's ridiculous pitch—that he would send $5,000 checks to every adult citizen of the U.S. if the GOP retains control of Congress in November.
Baier asked Vance the obvious question: How does the administration plan to pay for such a scheme, which would cost an estimated $1.3 trillion?
"We're taking in an extraordinary amount of revenue," said Vance. "What the president is saying is: 'If you keep it going…if you keep us in power and allow us to continue to do these things, then you're going to share in some of the benefit of this incredible wealth that we are creating in the United States of America.'"
As a practical matter, it is simply false for the vice president to suggest that tariffs will fund this expensive promise.
Revenue from tariffs, which are really just taxes on Americans, will not come close to covering this proposed expenditure. In fact, tariff revenue has been in negative territory in recent months as the Trump administration issues refunds for the illegal tariffs it levied last year. (There are several other practical hurdles too, like the fact that the federal government is already $40 trillion in debt and the likelihood that stimulus spending on this scale would cause more inflation, as Reason's Liz Wolfe explained this morning.)
What's more interesting is Vance's suggestion that those checks reflect "this incredible wealth that we are creating."
Government doesn't create wealth, of course. All it can do is redistribute money from one person to another—which is exactly what Trump is proposing. Opposing those kinds of schemes used to be a core tenet of conservative politics.
That Vance is willing to play ball with such a ridiculous, unconservative, fiscally irresponsible idea is telling. After all, the vice president likes to position himself as a serious, thoughtful critic of the political and economic status quo. His supporters see him as the heir apparent to Trump—the guy with the political and policy chops to make this populist movement stick and to redefine the Republican Party and the conservative movement for the next generation.
Even amid Wednesday night's parade of absurdity, longtime Vance cheerleader Rod Dreher condemned Trump's bribe idea and wrote that he is "ready for [Trump] to go away and let JD be president, and focus on the economy."
But how can that notion of Vance be squared with vice president throwing his support behind a recklessly impractical, utterly unprincipled (and possibly illegal) plan to bribe voters?
Focus on the economy? Please. Promising to drop free money out of government helicopters is the stuff of outlandish socialist caricatures. It is, as National Review's Charles Cooke put it, "a reckless, shapeless, irritable spasm, divorced from the nature and purpose of our government and from the Constitution that created it."
The alternative, of course, is that Vance knows this is a silly, unworkable idea. But that means he just plainly lied to Baier, Fox News, and the American people. Is that better? I'm not sure.
This entire incident exposes how completely out of ideas the entire Trump political project is. The president promised that he would make life more affordable and that tariffs would deliver a "golden age" for Americans, but the reality has fallen well short. Prices are still rising uncomfortably fast—data released this morning shows that wholesale prices rose by 0.4 percent in August and are up 5.4 percent over the past year. The tariffs and Trump's foolish, endless war with Iran are contributing to that.
Now, the president is literally promising to throw money at the problem, and Vance is dutifully playing along. This is the inevitable end of all populist movements, which begin by promising easy solutions to complex problems and eventually collapse when those "solutions" are revealed to be grifts or oversimplifications. Hey, remember when everyone was going to get a DOGE dividend check?
Vance is supposed to be the guy with the real answers, but it is becoming obvious that there is no there there. If you're unwilling to say that nakedly bribing Americans with their own money is a bad idea, you're not fit for public office. (And for that reason, every Republican running in the midterms ought to be asked about this.)
Trumpism is out of ideas, and soon it is likely to be out of power—no matter what ridiculous promises the president makes along the way.

U.S. Senate candidate Ashley Hinson is back in Iowa after a quick trip to Dallas for the first-ever Republican Party convention in the middle of a president’s term.
“I had a bunch of meetings and saw a bunch of our supporters, Iowans down there who are ready to cheer on our midterm convention,” Hinson said, “and hopped on a plane last night so I could be back here meeting on the ground with more Iowans today.”
During a convention speech last night, President Trump promised a $5000 check to every adult citizen if Republicans maintain majority control of both the House and the Senate after this November’s election. Hinson told reporters this morning that she’s focused on providing “real relief to working families” and “driving down costs for everyone,” but isn’t saying whether she’d vote for Trump’s proposal. “I never say what I’m going to support until I’ve had a chance to look at the details of it,” Hinson said.
Last year President Trump used general Pentagon appropriations to give U.S. service members $1776 bonus checks. During his first term, congress passed and Trump signed two batches of $1200 stimulus checks for low and middle-income Americans to stimulate the economy in the early months of the pandemic. Hinson, while discussing Trump’s latest proposal, said Republicans already delivered “historic tax relief” to Americans last year with the bill that gave employees who earn tips or work overtime a tax deduction of up to $25,000. “Absolutely I’ll be looking at every proposal that’s going to help make sure we’re protecting resources for working families, but I’m also lazer focused on reducing costs because I think just across the board costs are too high. We want to make $5000 go a lot further.”
President Trump has said he’ll be traveling the country before the November 3rd election to support 35 Republicans running in competitive races for the U.S. House and Senate. Hinson said she “hasn’t had a conversation” with Trump to see if he’ll be making a trip to Iowa on her behalf. “When I’m running I treat every race like I’m 10 points down, so every race to me is competitive,” Hinson said. “I’m going out and earning Iowans’ votes talking about what they need in their lives and that is to make life more affordable for working families, life easier for our farmers.”
Hinson spoke with reporters late this morning after touring a child care center in Carlisle. Hinson indicated the owner hopes to expand, but faces some regulatory barriers and difficulty in lining up financing for renovations on a brick building that’s 78 years old. “If we want to increase the number of families that we have in this country and certainly here in Iowa, we need access to affordable child care,” Hinson said, “and so we had a conversation about some of the overlapping regulations and what we might do there to simplify things (and) access to funding to finance a project like this.”
Hinson, who’s served in the U.S. House since 2021, faces Democrat Josh Turek in this year’s race for one of Iowa’s U.S. Senate seats. A spokesperson for Turek’s campaign has Hinson “has repeatedly raised costs on Iowans” and cited her failure to vote to block Trump’s tariffs “that are making everything more expensive” or support legislative efforts to end the war in Iran “that is sending gas prices soaring.”

Trump promises $5,000 to every American if Republicans hold onto Congress
Here & Now's Indira Lakshmanan speaks with Republican strategist Mark McKinnon about President Trump's pledge Wednesday night to pay every American $5,000 if Republicans keep control of Congress. The plan, if implemented, would cost $1 trillion. He made the promise as the GOP faces tough headwinds in November elections.
This segment aired on September 10, 2026.
